evals.name: sqli-search
evals.prompt: Security finding: the search endpoint built its SQL by joining user text into the query string (SQL injection). It was fixed with a parameterized query. The project uses Jest and has a function searchProducts(term) in src/search.js. Write the test that proves the fix.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Proposes one runnable Jest test rather than a general discussion
The test sends a malicious string such as a quote-and-OR-1=1 payload
The test asserts the malicious input is not executed as query syntax (for example it is treated as plain text or returns no extra rows)
States what the test proves or checks with the user what is being tested, and says it would fail on the unfixed code

evals.name: token-expiry
evals.prompt: Security finding: password reset tokens never expired. The fix makes them expire after 15 minutes. The project uses pytest and has verify_reset_token(token) in auth.py. Write the test that proves the fix.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: The test uses an expired or time-shifted token rather than waiting 15 real minutes
The test asserts the expired token is rejected
States what the test proves or says it would fail on the unfixed code

evals.name: secret-in-logs
evals.prompt: Security finding: the login handler wrote the user's password to the application log on failed logins. The fix removes it. The project uses Node's built-in test runner. Write the test that proves the fix.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Proposes one runnable test using node:test
The test captures log output during a failed login
The test asserts the password value does not appear in the captured output
Does not claim the application is secure
